title: How Do Neural Networks Learn? Deep Learning Fundamentals Explained

cues.en: Instructor: Hello and welcome back to the course on deep learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到深度學習。

cues.en: Now that we've seen neural networks in action, it's time for us to find out how they learn.
cues.zh: 看過網路運作，現在了解如何學習。

cues.en: So let's dive straight into it.
There are two fundamentally different approaches to getting a program to do what you want it to do.
cues.zh: 讓程式完成目標，有兩個根本不同方法。

cues.en: One is hard coded coding where you actually tell the program specific rules and what outcomes you want, and you just guide it throughout the whole way
cues.zh: 一個硬式編碼，明確告訴規則、要什麼結果，全程引導，

cues.en: and you account for all the possible options that the program has to deal with.
cues.zh: 考慮它要處理的一切選項。

cues.en: On the other hand, you have neural networks where you create a facility for the program to be able to understand what it needs to do
cues.zh: 另一個神經網路，建立設施，讓程式自行了解

cues.en: on its own.
So you basically create this neural network where you provide it inputs, you tell it what you want as outputs, and then you let it figure everything out on its own.
cues.zh: 基本上建立網路，給輸入、告訴想要輸出，再讓它自己摸索。

cues.en: Two fundamentally different approaches, and that is something to keep in mind as we go through these tutorials.
Our goal is to create this network which then learns on its own.
cues.zh: 目標是建能自行學習的網路。

cues.en: We are going to avoid trying to put in the rules.
And a good example that I can give you right now is, this will come further in the course, but it's just a very visual example.
cues.zh: 舉個很直觀、後面會介紹的例。

cues.en: For instance, how do you distinguish between a dog and a cat?
For on the left side on the approach that's depicted on the left, you would program things in like the cat's ears have to be like this.
cues.zh: 左側方法，編碼貓耳要這樣。

cues.en: Look out for whiskers.
Look out for this type of nose.
Look out for this type of shape of face.
Look out for these colors.
You kind of, you'd describe all these things and you'd have conditions like if the ears are pointy, then cat.
cues.zh: 描述全部，再寫耳尖就是貓。

cues.en: If the ears are sloping down, then possibly dog and so on.
On the other hand, for a neural network, you just code the neural network.
So you code the architecture and then you point the neural network at a folder with all these cats and dogs, with images of cats and dogs which are already categorized.
cues.zh: 寫架構，再指向已分類貓狗圖片資料夾。

cues.en: And you tell it, Okay, I've got you.
I've got some images of cats and dogs.
Go and learn what a cat is.
Go and learn what a dog is.
And the neural network will, on its own, understand everything it needs to understand.
cues.zh: 網路自行理解所需一切。

cues.en: And then further down, once it's trained up, when you give it a new image of a cat or a dog, it'll be able to understand what it was.
cues.zh: 訓練好，給新貓狗圖，就知道是什麼。

cues.en: So there they are.
Those are the two fundamentally different approaches and today we're going to slowly start getting into how that second approach works.
cues.zh: 根本不同方法，今天慢慢介紹第二種。

cues.en: All right.
So let's get straight to it.
Here, we have a very basic neural network with a one layer.
This is called a single layer feed forward neural network and it is also called a perceptron.
cues.zh: 叫單層前饋神經網路，也叫感知器。

cues.en: Now, before we proceed, one thing that we do need to adjust is that output value.
Right now you can see that it's just a y.
We need to put a yhat in there.
And the reason for that is usually y stands for the actual value.
cues.zh: 因 y 通常代表真實值。

cues.en: And that's what we're going to be using.
So y is gonna be the actual value, which we see in reality.
Output value is the predicted value by the algorithm, by the neural network.
cues.zh: 輸出是演算法、網路預測值。

cues.en: Yhat is the output value.
Basically that's the denomination for the output value.
And the perceptron was first invented in 1957 by Frank Rosenblatt and his whole idea was to create something that can actually learn
cues.zh: 感知器由 Frank Rosenblatt 於 1957 發明，想創造能學習

cues.en: and adjust itself.
And this is what we're going to be looking at now.
So we've got our perceptron.
Let's see how our perceptron learns.
So let's say we have some input values that have been supplied to the perceptron and, or basically to our neural network.
cues.zh: 假設輸入值已提供給感知器、網路。

cues.en: Then the activation functions applied, we have an output.
And now we're going to plot the output on a chart.
So there it is our output yhat.
Now what we need to do is, in order to be able to learn, we need to compare the output value to the actual value that we want the neural network to get, right?
cues.zh: 要學習，必須比較輸出和希望網路取得的真實值。

cues.en: And that is the value y.
And so if we plot it here, you'll see that there's a bit of a difference.
Now we are going to calculate a function called the cost function.
It's calculated as one half of the difference, of the square difference between the actual value and output value.
cues.zh: 真實與輸出差的平方，再乘二分之一。

cues.en: Now there are many ways you can come up for cost function.
There are many different cost functions that you can use.
This is probably the most commonly used cost function.
And why it is specifically this function we use, we'll find out further down when we're talking about gradient descent.
cues.zh: 為何特別用它，梯度下降時會知道。

cues.en: But for now we're just going to agree that this is the cost function.
cues.zh: 目前約定這是成本函數。

cues.en: And basically what the cost function is telling us is what is the error that you have in your prediction?
cues.zh: 告訴我們預測誤差多少。

cues.en: And our goal is to minimize the cost function, because the lower the cost function, the closer the yhat is to y.
cues.zh: 目標最小化，越低 ŷ 越近 y。

cues.en: Okay, so as long as we agree on that, let's proceed.
So basically from here, what happens is there's our cost function.
And from here, what happens is now we are going to, once we've compared, now we're going to feed this information back into the neural network.
cues.zh: 比較後，把資訊回饋網路。

cues.en: So there we go.
There's the information going back into the neural network and it goes to the weights and the weights get updated.
Basically, the only thing that we have control of in this very simple neural network are the weights, W1, W2, all the way to Wm.
cues.zh: 簡單網路唯一可控，是 w₁、w₂ 到 wₘ 權重。

cues.en: And our goal is to minimize the cost function.
So all we can do is update the weight.
So we update the weights, tweak them a little bit and how exactly, we'll find out further down.
But for now, we agree that we update the weights and then we continue.
So, but here I've put up this screenshot of the data just to make one point very clear.
cues.zh: 放資料截圖，是要說清一點。

cues.en: That, right now, throughout this whole experiment, everything we're doing right now, we're dealing with just the one row.
cues.zh: 整個實驗目前，只處理一列。

cues.en: So we're dealing with, we have a data set of one row where we have, for instance, we're dealing with how long you study.
cues.zh: 一列資料，例如處理讀書多久。

cues.en: Like the variable that we're predicting is what results you're gonna get on an exam.
And the independent variables that we have is how many hours did you study for?
How many hours did you sleep and what did you get on the quiz in the mid-semester?
cues.zh: 睡幾小時、期中小考得分。

cues.en: So in the middle of the semester, there's a quiz, what percentage did you get there?
cues.zh: 學期中小考得幾百分比？

cues.en: So based on those variables, we're trying to predict what score you'll get for the exam.
cues.zh: 根據這些預測考試分數。

cues.en: And in exam, the 93%, that's the actual value.
So that's y.
So we feed these three values into our neural network again for the second time now.
And then we're going to be comparing the result to y.
So let's see how this works.
We feed these values into the neural network.
Everything gets adjusted and weights get adjusted.
So as you can see, let's do this again.
We're going to feed the values again.
The point here is that we're feeding in these same values.
So we only have one row.
We're trying to, we're training on one row.
This is because this is just a very simple basic example.
Then we'll see what happens when there's more rows.
So again, we feed these rows in.
Our cost functions get adjusted.
As you can see, everything happens along those lines again.
So as you can see, every time our yhat is changing, because we've tweaked the weights, our yhat is changing, our cost function's changing.
cues.zh: 每次因為調權重，ŷ 改，成本也改。

cues.en: Let's have a look again.
So, we feed those in.
Yhat is changing, cost function is changing.
We get information back, feedback to the weights, so that the weights get adjusted again.
We feed in the same values every time.
Everything gets adjusted.
Goes back to the weights.
And one more time.
We feed in.
Okay?
And another time.
So we've adjusted the weights.
We feed in the information, and there we go.
So now this time the yhat is equal to y, cost function is zero.
cues.zh: 這次 ŷ 等於 y，成本 0。

cues.en: Usually you won't get cost function equal to zero.
But this is a very simple example.
So hopefully all that made sense.
Every time we feed in exactly that same row, because just, in this case, we're just dealing with that one row into our neural network where then the weights,
cues.zh: 每次輸入完全相同列，因為只處理這一列，網路裡權重，

cues.en: the value get value supplied, but the weights the activation functions applied.
cues.zh: 對輸入值加權，再套活化。

cues.en: We get yhat.
Yhat is compared to y.
Then we see how the cost function has changed.
Feedback, feed that information back into the neural network and adjust, adjust the weights again.
cues.zh: 資訊回饋網路，再調權重。

cues.en: And then we repeat the same process again with the same exact row.
We're trying to minimize that cost function.
So up until now, we've been dealing with just that one row.
Let's see what happens when you have multiple rows.
So here's the full data set.
We have eight rows of how many hours you slept or maybe these are different students in taking the same exam.
cues.zh: 八列，睡多久，可能是考同一考試的不同學生。

cues.en: How many others hours they studied?
How many hours they slept before the exam?
What they get on the quiz and their final result on the test.
And as you can see here, on the left I've got eight of these perceptrons.
Actually, they are all the same perceptron.
So this is also important to understand.
I just multiplied it or like duplicated eight times just so that we can conceptually understand.
cues.zh: 只是複製八次，便於理解。

cues.en: But the important thing here, it's the same neural network.
We're going to be feeding these into one same neural network.
So let's go.
Let's get started.
So one epoch, as you'll hear Hedland mentioning.
One epoch is when we go through a whole data set and we train our neural network on all of these rows.
cues.zh: 一個 epoch，就是走完整個資料集，訓練所有列。

cues.en: So let's go, let's get started.
So there's our first row.
And there's yhat for the first row.
There's the second row.
There's yhat for the second row.
So again, it's being fed into the same neural network every time.
I've just copied them several times, so we can visually see how this is happening.
Then again, it's happening again.
That's third row, fourth row.
There's our yhat for the fourth row and so on.
Basically, then we get the same values for the remaining four rows, as well.
cues.zh: 其餘四列也得到對應值。

cues.en: So every time we just feed in a row into our neural network, we get a value.
cues.zh: 每次輸入一列，就一個值。

cues.en: Then we compare to the actual values.
So there are the actual values.
So for every single row, we have an actual value.
And now based on all of these differences between yhat and y, we can calculate the cost function, which is the sum of all of those squared differences
cues.zh: 根據所有 ŷ 與 y 差異，算成本，所有平方差

cues.en: between yhat and y, and all of that is halved.
And there's our cost function.
And basically now what we do after we have the full cost function, we go back and we update the weights.
cues.zh: 完整成本算好，回頭更新權重。

cues.en: We update W1, W2, W3.
And the important thing to remember here is that all of these perceptrons, all of these neural networks is actually one neural network.
cues.zh: 記得這些感知器、網路，其實只有一個。

cues.en: So there's not eight of them, there's just one.
And when we update the weights, we're going to update the weights in that one neural network.
cues.zh: 更新的是同一網路權重。

cues.en: So basically the weights are gonna be the same for all of the rows.
cues.zh: 基本上所有列權重相同。

cues.en: So it's not the case that every row has its own weights.
Now all the rows share the weights.
And so that's why we looked at the cost function, which is the sum of the square differences.
cues.zh: 所以看平方差總和的成本。

cues.en: And then we updated the weights.
And now from here, that was just one iteration.
Next, we're going to run this whole thing again.
We're going to feed every single row into the neural network.
Find out our cost function and do this whole process again.
So just as we saw previously where we had just one row and we were doing everything again and again, again, again.
Same thing here.
But now we're gonna be doing it for eight rows or 800 rows or 8,000 rows.
However many rows you have in your data set.
You do this process and then you calculate the cost function.
And the goal here is to minimize the cost function and to get, as soon as you found the minimum of the cost function, that is your final neural network.
cues.zh: 目標最小化，找到最小成本，就是最終網路。

cues.en: That means your weights have been adjusted and you have found the optimal weights
for this data set that you're training on.
cues.zh: 此訓練資料集最佳權重。

cues.en: And you're ready to proceed to the testing phase or to the application phase.
And this whole process is called back propagation.
cues.zh: 這整個過程叫反向傳播。

It's actually got some good examples and application or use cases for different cost functions.

And on that note, I hope you enjoy today's tutorial.
I look forward to seeing you next time.
Until then, enjoy deep learning.
